meta.title: LibreRythmo: free dubbing studio, rythmo band and voice recording
meta.description: LibreRythmo is a free, open-source dubbing studio: frame-accurate rythmo band design, multi-take voice recording per character, one character's voice muted so their part can be acted, an automatic voice chain and a dubbed video out. Windows, macOS and Linux.
meta.keywords: rythmo band, dubbing studio, free dubbing software, dubbing recording, rythmo band editor, dubbing software, lip sync, DETX, fandub, remove vocals, dubbing transcription, open source dubbing

hero.title: The simple, free dubbing studio.
hero.subtitle: The smoothest rythmo band design there is, and now the rest of the craft: a character's voice mutes so their part can be acted inside the real soundtrack, every take lands on the scrolling band, and the video comes out dubbed. **Free**, **blazing fast**, **no video length limit**. Windows, macOS and Linux.

what.title: Dubbing end to end, in a single app.
what.body: A rythmo band is the scrolling strip of text that runs under the picture in a dubbing studio, stretched so each word lands exactly on the actor's lips. LibreRythmo brings that technique to everyone, and version 3 adds the other half of the craft: a recording mode where each character has their own take track, where their original voice drops out during their lines, and where the video comes out dubbed. No subscription, no length limit, no dated interface.

features.title: Per-word timing, snapped to the lips.
features.body: Timing adjusts word by word and every boundary lands on the lips, down to the frame, with the magnet catching edges to help. To move fast, multi-selection changes the character, font or voice-over across dozens of lines at once, proportional stretching keeps everything straight across 1 to 4 tracks, and adjustable silences slip in where needed. The finest sync possible, without fighting the tool.
features.alt: Frame-accurate word adjustment on the LibreRythmo rythmo band

features.title: Butter-smooth scrubbing, even in 4K or HEVC.
features.body: The wheel glides the band along the audio, frame by frame, without a single hitch. A 720p proxy generated and cached in the background makes any source instant regardless of codec, while the export starts over from the full-quality original. Feedback is immediate: the design keeps up with the pace of thought.
features.alt: LibreRythmo fullscreen playback with the composited rythmo band

features.title: One-key reacs, fonts embedded in the project.
features.body: A reac (ah, oh, fff, (laughs)…) drops in with a single key or from the palette, a line switches to underlined voice-over, and every actor has their own colour, selectable from keys 1 to 9. Each line can also carry its own font: any TTF/OTF embeds into the .rythmo, which keeps its fonts once shared, on top of the bundled open fonts (Inter, Oswald, Comfortaa, Anton).
features.alt: Character panel and reac palette in LibreRythmo

features.title: Automatic shot detection, live scene stats.
features.body: LibreRythmo spots shot changes on its own (ffmpeg) and drops the markers on the timeline: not a single cut slips by. Scene slicing shows live counters (lines, duration, characters), OUT segments flag stretches with nothing to dub, and navigation jumps scene to scene from the keyboard.
features.alt: Scene markers and shot detection on the LibreRythmo timeline

features.title: The text starts from the audio, one character per voice.
features.body: Retyping a whole episode takes hours: transcription roughs out the work locally, slices the audio into lines, detects the speakers and creates one character per voice, in the chosen language. The engine and models install in one click from Settings, run without a connection, and nothing is forced: the app stays light until they are needed.
features.alt: LibreRythmo assisted transcription window with model and language choice

features.title: Each character on their track, each pass in takes.
features.body: The band scrolls in final-render mode and recording starts from the playhead, take after take: overlapping ones stack up, the keeper is a click away, and any take trims or moves freely. Hardware latency is compensated so the voice lands where it was performed, and the voice chain (EQ, de-esser, plosive tamer, compression, loudness aligned to the video) fires from a single FX button.
features.alt: LibreRythmo recording mode: takes per character under the rythmo band

features.title: Their voice mutes, the rest of the mix keeps playing.
features.body: The built-in voice remover produces an instrumental track, locally. During a muted character's lines, monitoring switches over to it: their voice disappears while the music, effects and other actors stay in place. Rehearsing and recording happen inside the real soundtrack, not on top of it, and comparing with the original is one click away.
features.alt: LibreRythmo dubbing monitor: one character's voice muted onto the voiceless track

features.title: DETX, PDF, GPU MP4: the video comes out dubbed.
features.body: In: DETX (Joker / Cappella), SRT / ASS / VTT, or a YouTube video downloaded directly. Out: a DETX, PDF work documents, a ZIP of the recordings mixed per character, or a fully composited MP4 encoded on the GPU (NVENC, QuickSync, AMF, x264 fallback) with the chosen characters' takes mixed in, raw or processed. The band can even be left out, to deliver the dubbed video alone.
features.alt: LibreRythmo MP4 export window with recordings mix and GPU encoding

why.title: Built by a dubbing enthusiast, for everyone.
why.body: LibreRythmo was born because every existing tool was either too old, clumsy to use, or locked behind a subscription that limited video length. And once the band was designed, recording it still required another program: version 3 brings both halves of dubbing into the same window, heavily optimized and entirely free.

points.title: Free forever
points.body: No subscription, no duration limit, no paywall. Open source, GPL-3 licensed.

points.title: Fast and light
points.body: Heavily optimized to stay smooth even on an ordinary machine, from design to export.

points.title: Everything local
points.body: Transcription and voice removal run on the machine, with no connection and no account. Models install only if wanted.

points.title: Made for creators
points.body: Ideal for fandub communities, associations and semi-pro work: it speaks the professional standards.

items.q: What is a rythmo band editor?
items.a: A rythmo band editor lets you write text on a strip scrolling under the video and stretch each word so it sticks to the actor's lips. It is the standard dubbing technique. LibreRythmo is a free, open-source rythmo band editor for Windows, macOS and Linux, which also records the voices.
Yes. LibreRythmo is entirely free and open source, GPL-3 licensed, with no subscription, no watermark and no video duration limit. It will stay free forever.

items.q: Can I record my voice in it?
items.a: Yes, that is what the recording mode is for: each character has their own track, takes stack up so the best one can be kept, microphone latency is compensated, and an automatic voice chain (EQ, de-esser, compression, leveling) applies from one button. The recordings are mixed into the exported video or delivered as a per-character ZIP.

items.q: How do I act a character's part without hearing their voice?
items.a: The built-in voice remover produces an instrumental track locally. With a character muted, playback switches to that track during their lines: their voice disappears while the music, effects and other actors stay in place.

A composited MP4 with GPU encoding, with or without the band, with the chosen characters' recordings mixed in; a per-character ZIP of the recordings; PDF work documents (presence grid, line tally); a DETX file (Joker and Cappella compatible) and subtitles (SRT / ASS / VTT).

items.q: Do transcription and voice removal need the Internet?
items.a: No. Both run entirely on the machine, with no account and no connection. Nothing ships in the app by default: engines and models install in one click from Settings, only when needed.
Windows (installer or portable zip), macOS (Apple Silicon .dmg) and Linux (AppImage, .deb and .pacman). The interface is available in English, French and Spanish.
Yes. LibreRythmo builds a cached 720p proxy in the background so heavy 4K and HEVC sources stay smooth while editing, and regenerates the export from the full-quality original.

items.q: Is it a good alternative to paid dubbing tools?
items.a: LibreRythmo speaks industry-standard formats like DETX, exports professional work documents and covers voice recording: it fits amateur, fandub and semi-professional workflows, without the cost or duration limits of many paid or online tools.
